correctness.rationale: For any connected simple triangle-free H with n>=2,m>=1, T=L(S(H)) has oriented-incidence vertices (v,w), disjoint clique blocks C_v and reversal edges. Adams odd/even facet formula gives K₂=<C_v∪{(w,v)}> and K₃ generated by B_vw=C_v∪C_w plus C_v with a pair (w,v),(z,v). For each pair of different neighbors the external marker is unique because H has no triangle, so descending-size toggles are elementary free-face removals K₃⇘K₀=<B_vw>. Faces of K₀ outside K₂ have nonempty proper incidence subsets from both edge endpoints and a unique edge block; descending-size toggles give K₀⇘K₂. Further edge-centered toggles give K₂⇘R₀ (the disjoint clique simplices and reversal edges); collapsing each C_v to a star tree gives a graph that contracts its internal forests to H. Inclusion K₂↪K₃ is therefore a simple-homotopy equivalence and H₁ integral iso. Scale1→2 kills exactly the independent internal cycle lattices ∑_v H₁(K_deg(v);Z), rank ∑_v binom(deg(v)-1,2). Independent finite constructions checked paths, stars, C₄, K₂,₃, and the C₃ counterexample has mod-two H₂:0 at scale2 and 2 at scale3. The proof is general; finite checks cannot establish its quantifier.

value.rationale: The result identifies a non-obvious persistence interval for an infinite natural graph operation (vertex truncation/line graph of subdivision), with explicit inclusion-preserving collapses rather than homology-rank coincidences. The triangle obstruction H=C₃ demonstrates a natural boundary, and the surviving exact integral inclusion behavior can inform graph-metric Čech persistence studies. It is not accepted on strength of already known scale-two consequences.
